# `silk/core/static_text`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Operations on string literals during static evaluation: length, byte access, concatenation, and
slices.

## When to use
Use [`StaticText`](#StaticText) to check or build text at compile time, such as to parse a format template
and report an error in the compiler. Use `silk.text.string.String` for text at runtime.

## Details
The operations work on UTF-8 bytes. They run only during static evaluation. The results are
static values, so they add no runtime cost.

## Examples
### Measure a literal at compile time
```silk
import silk.core.static_text { StaticText }

static fn greeting() -> string<'static> {
  return StaticText.concat("hello, ", "world")
}

static fn greetingLength() -> usize {
  return StaticText.byteLength(greeting())
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let length = greetingLength()
  if length != 12 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `StaticText` with `import silk.core.static_text { StaticText }`.

## `StaticText`

```silk
pub struct StaticText
```

The owner type of the static text operations. It has no fields and is never constructed.

### Details

Each operation is `static`. It runs only during static evaluation, such as in a `static fn`, a
`static for`, or a `const` initializer.

## Implementation `StaticText`

```silk
impl StaticText
```

<a id="StaticText.impl.byteLength"></a>

### Associated function `byteLength`

```silk
pub static fn byteLength(value: string) -> usize
```

Returns the number of UTF-8 bytes in `value`. This is not the number of characters.

<a id="StaticText.impl.byteAt"></a>

### Associated function `byteAt`

```silk
pub static fn byteAt(value: string, index: usize) -> u8
```

Returns the UTF-8 byte at the zero-based byte position `index` of `value`.

#### Gotchas

If `index` is not less than [`StaticText.byteLength`](#StaticText.impl.byteLength), static evaluation stops and the
compiler reports an error.

<a id="StaticText.impl.concat"></a>

### Associated function `concat`

```silk
pub static fn concat(left: string, right: string) -> string<'static>
```

Returns `left` followed by `right`.

#### Details

A compiler error about the result points to the source location of `left`.

<a id="StaticText.impl.slice"></a>

### Associated function `slice`

```silk
pub static fn slice(value: string, start: usize, end: usize) -> string<'static>
```

Returns the bytes of `value` from byte position `start` to byte position `end`, with `end` not
included.

#### Gotchas

`start` and `end` must be at character boundaries, with `start <= end <= byteLength(value)`.
Otherwise, static evaluation stops and the compiler reports an error.
